TextBlock.Text: THEATRE Banda approaches, north of Tanimbar
DATE 21 October 2028 · 1040 local
SIDE Royal Australian Navy
WINDOW 100 min, closes at 150
Arafura-class OPV (stand-in). Photo: VolgaDnper1488 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · cropped
"Saying so, unfortunately, does not make it true; and if true, saying so does not always make it believed."
- Thomas C. Schelling

BANDA APPROACHES, NORTH OF TANIMBAR, 1040. MV Kota Meridian, a logistics merchant under a Meridian escort boat, has been working north from the Arafura since dawn. Signals intelligence expects a handover to a second ship somewhere north of the Tanimbar group this afternoon, and three ships are waiting there: two Indonesian traders and a trawler, any of which could be the receiver.

HMAS Eyre has two uncrewed boats in company. KRAKEN 1 is the RAN's own K5, three months in service; CORSAIR 41 is a Saronic Corsair the US Navy lent the RAN for the fortnight. Both are unarmed, both are quick, and neither has anyone aboard to lose.

Identify the receiver and put a boat within three miles of the handover. The escort boat is weapons tight; so are you. Keep Eyre out of its sight if you can: a Meridian report naming an Australian warship off Tanimbar is a story Canberra does not want this week.
COMMAND NET: A mission-specific tactical report follows eight minutes after the start. It is advice from the command team, not a new sensor detection.
Commodore Alex Mercer; Lieutenant Commander Dana Whitlock, RAN uncrewed systems, for the boats
COMMANDER'S INTENT

This is a week before anyone is allowed to shoot, and I want it to stay that way. The merchant has an escort and the escort has a radar. Keep Eyre over its horizon and let the boats do the looking: they are small, fast and nobody's sailors. Put a name on whoever takes the cargo and a boat inside three miles of the handover so we have it on camera. Nobody fires at anything.
• Identify the receiver, then put a boat within three miles of the handover
• Keep HMAS Eyre unidentified by Meridian
• Do not fire on the merchant
• Harm no lane traffic

HMAS Eyre with KRAKEN 1 (RAN) and CORSAIR 41 (US Navy, on loan). Opposing, neither of them firing: MV Kota Meridian, one Meridian escort boat and the receiver, which is one of three ships at the handover. Neutral: lane traffic.

The planned window is 100 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 50 minutes more; the operation is closed at 150 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
All designated neutral contacts are protected. A protected neutral loss cancels the operation. Identify before you shoot.
